### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SaveMetaItemRequest (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ExecutionContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const), handleMetadataRequest (symbol, a top-level function), handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function), registerMetaItemHistoryRoutes (symbol, a top-level function), registerMetaItemWriteRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via publishPackageDrafts (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation; a method of class ProtocolHistoryAndPublishFacet))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `38ab69949dd684852f4698bd70f7b56932a4bb27` — the merge of head `1cffbad85e173c44382e98e866f69639619a5628` into base `e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 38ab69949dd684852f4698bd70f7b56932a4bb27 && git checkout 38ab69949dd684852f4698bd70f7b56932a4bb27
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee 1cffbad85e173c44382e98e866f69639619a5628 && git checkout -B drift-repro e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee && git merge --no-ff 1cffbad85e173c44382e98e866f69639619a5628

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `caeb90463be47d31b3e87f0d4f1880ea943787e2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts + packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/kernel.json, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-door-requests.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **Schema (hits).** `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema` and `PublishMetaItemRequestSchema` gain an optional `userTextLocales` (array of strings, max 2). `ExecutionContextSchema` gains an optional `workspaceLocale`. Both are additive and optional, so nothing accepted before is refused. At this head the batch body `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema` is unchanged: its door passes the locales to `publishPackageDrafts` directly, and a body `userTextLocales` is pinned as not read. That is the right call, because that schema is the body parser.
- **Server-stated, never from a wire body.** Both save doors build the request field by field: `meta-item-write-routes.ts` (the existing "never spreads the body" comment) and `runtime/domains/meta.ts`. Both set `userTextLocales: userTextLocalesOf(ctx)` from the resolved execution context, the `client` precedent. The closed-set and member-selector pins were updated to include it. A client cannot choose another caller's language or smuggle a value in. The value only selects a language, and no verdict depends on it (stated in the schema description and in the gate's jsdoc).
- **Context.** `workspaceLocale` is filled only for a non-anonymous principal from `localization.locale`, beside the existing fold `locale`. `userTextLocalesOf` returns `[locale, workspaceLocale]` without empties. When no request locale is named, both rungs are the workspace default. That is harmless: the producer tries each once.
- **Gate.** `issueOf(locales)` adds `userMessage` only when the rule authors a sentence (`findingUserMessage`, #32790's catalog). The other six keys are copied unchanged. Threading through save, single publish and package publish is pass-through only.
- nit N1: `Metadata-protocol: added` sits beside a `Skills-docs: none` reason that says nothing is authored. If `added` is there because the authorable-surface baseline (`api.json`, `kernel.json`) moved, say that in one clause. Otherwise `none` fits the stated reason better.
- nit N2 (follow-up): other metadata write doors (MCP tools, CLI) state no locales and compose `en`. That is fine for now; it's worth one line in the changeset or a p3 card.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor` for two additive optional members, patch elsewhere. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is correct. No refusal is added and no member is removed (the batch body member was withdrawn before landing).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Published schema: `packages/spec/src/**`. Generated references are regenerated per the body.
- Shared files with E1 (`protocol.ts`, `protocol-save.ts`, `protocol-history-and-publish.ts`): pass-through lines only. The body checked them against E1's open PR #33251. Re-check at landing whether E1 merged first.
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); area A2 session_016WV4cz2MxDkQYCC4U8indM.
- CI at this head when read: 14 green, 23 running, 1 cancelled (superseded), none red. The previous head was red, so the ACCEPT must see every check green at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Ruling C on #32440 puts sentence composition at the producer, with the request's language, then the workspace default, then `en`. The protocol never sees the request, so the door has to state both rungs. Keeping `locale` as the fold and adding `workspaceLocale` as the unfolded second rung is the smallest schema change that makes the ladder possible. Declaring the member server-stated on the request schema matches the `client` precedent. Holds against the cited code and the ruling's scenario (an unsupported request locale falls back to the workspace default, pinned with `tlh`).
